1.web: Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery. The prey doesn’t depart.
1.asv: Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and rapine; the prey departeth not.

2.web: The noise of the whip, the noise of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots,
2.asv: The noise of the whip, and the noise of the rattling of wheels, and prancing horses, and bounding chariots,

3.web: the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies,
3.asv: the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, and the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies; they stumble upon their bodies;—

4.web: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
4.asv: because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the well-favored harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.

5.web: “Behold, I am against you,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
5.asv: Behold, I am against thee, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will uncover thy skirts upon thy face; and I will show the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.

6.web: I will throw abominable filth on you, and make you vile, and will set you a spectacle.
6.asv: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazing-stock.

7.web: It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”
7.asv: And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?

8.web: Are you better than No-Amon, who was situated among the rivers, who had the waters around her; whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?
8.asv: Art thou better than No-amon, that was situate among the rivers, that had the waters round about her; whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?

9.web: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength. Put and Libya were her helpers.
9.asv: Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers.

10.web: Yet was she carried away. She went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
10.asv: Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity; her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets; and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.

11.web: You also will be drunken. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
11.asv: Thou also shalt be drunken; thou shalt be hid; thou also shalt seek a stronghold because of the enemy.

12.web: All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
12.asv: All thy fortresses shall be like fig-trees with the first-ripe figs: if they be shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.

13.web: Behold, your troops in your midst are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies. The fire has devoured your bars.
13.asv: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women; the gates of thy land are set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire hath devoured thy bars.

14.web: Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
14.asv: Draw thee water for the siege; strengthen thy fortresses; go into the clay, and tread the mortar; make strong the brickkiln.

15.web: There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
15.asv: There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off; it shall devour thee like the canker-worm: make thyself many as the canker-worm; make thyself many as the locust.

16.web: You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips, and flees away.
16.asv: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the canker-worm ravageth, and fleeth away.

17.web: Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
17.asv: Thy princes are as the locusts, and thy marshals as the swarms of grasshoppers, which encamp in the hedges in the cold day, but when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.

18.web: Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
18.asv: Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; thy nobles are at rest; thy people are scattered upon the mountains, and there is none to gather them.

19.web: There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you; for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?
19.asv: There is no assuaging of thy hurt; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the report of thee clap their hands over thee; for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
